rulings.found: Similarly enamoured with high-wire wordless singing, Fraser was often cited as an influence on Birgisson at the start of his career, only he’d never heard a note of her music.
rulings.citation: The Guardian (18 Aug 2020): Jónsi Birgisson had never heard Cocteau Twins at the start of his career, despite the comparisons, and only listened to them years later.
rulings.why: The page says Jónsi had not heard them when the comparison was made, so the influence did not run.

rulings.found: it was Faust who served as the weirdo Dada-informed distant cousin more interested in improvisation and poetry, undoubtedly the muse unto which Sonic Youth owes royalties.
rulings.citation: Vice argued that Faust was "undoubtedly the muse unto which Sonic Youth owes royalties."
rulings.why: A critic asserts Sonic Youth drew on Faust, a passing but direct claim (close call).

rulings.found: “‘Sister Ray’ is the ultimate song,” he said. “Maybe you can’t call it a song – the ultimate noise statement of all time: there’s never been a song like that and there never will be again. It is with me always.”
rulings.citation: Stephen Malkmus told The Observer in 2013 (reported by NME) that the Velvet Underground's "Sister Ray" is "the ultimate song... It is with me always."
rulings.why: Malkmus says the song has stayed with him always, close to the keep-listening test (closest call; fandom stated after the split).
